faqs_subtitle: Everything you need to know about running vector databases with KubeDB

faqs.question: Which vector databases does KubeDB support?
faqs.answer: KubeDB provides operators for Qdrant, Milvus, and Weaviate, and supports the pgvector extension on PostgreSQL. The documentation lists the supported versions for each engine.

faqs.question: Should I use a dedicated vector database or pgvector?
faqs.answer: Use pgvector when embeddings belong next to relational data and you want to query both with SQL in one database. Use Qdrant, Milvus, or Weaviate when vector search is its own workload, especially for large or fast-growing collections. KubeDB lets you run both side by side.

faqs.question: Can I run these databases in a distributed topology?
faqs.answer: Yes. Qdrant supports distributed mode with Raft consensus, Milvus supports standalone and distributed topologies with external object storage and KubeDB-managed or external etcd, and Weaviate runs as a multi-node cluster.

faqs.question: How do I back up my embeddings?
faqs.answer: KubeDB provides backup and restore for every vector engine it supports. Qdrant supports logical backup and volume snapshots, Milvus supports base backup, volume snapshots, and point-in-time recovery, and PostgreSQL with pgvector has encrypted, incremental backups with point-in-time recovery. Backups go to any S3-compatible object store.

faqs.question: How do I enable pgvector?
faqs.answer: Deploy PostgreSQL with an extension-enabled PostgresVersion, then run CREATE EXTENSION vector in your database. You can then create vector columns and HNSW or IVFFlat indexes.

faqs.question: Does KubeDB host my embedding model or LLM?
faqs.answer: No. KubeDB runs the data layer: vector and relational databases. Your embedding model and LLM run wherever you choose, such as your own inference service or a provider API.

faqs.question: Can I keep everything inside my own network?
faqs.answer: Yes. KubeDB is self-hosted, so vector data stays in your cluster, and it supports air-gapped installation for isolated environments. See the air-gapped solution for details.

faqs.question: How do I scale as my corpus grows?
faqs.answer: Use ops requests for vertical and horizontal scaling and volume expansion, or enable the autoscaler for compute and storage. Scaling support varies by engine, so check the engine guide for details.

faqs.question: What about disaster recovery for pgvector databases?
faqs.answer: Because pgvector runs on PostgreSQL, it inherits KubeDB PostgreSQL high availability and cross-data-center disaster recovery, with near-zero RPO and RTO. See the BCDR solution for options.

faqs.question: Can I manage vector databases with GitOps?
faqs.answer: Yes. KubeDB provides GitOps support for all of its databases, including Qdrant, Milvus, Weaviate, and PostgreSQL with pgvector, so you can keep database definitions in Git. See the GitOps solution for the workflow.
